 Compound interest is “interest on interest.” You earn interest not only on the original amount you put in (the principal), but also on the interest that has already been added.

 Recipe: Leftover Chicken Fried Rice (15–20 minutes)

Ingredients (serves 2–3)
- 2 cups cooked rice (best if cold)
- 1–2 cups leftover cooked chicken, chopped or shredded
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (or 1 tbsp oil + 1 tbsp butter)
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1 cup mixed vegetables (frozen peas/carrots/corn or chopped fresh)
- 2–3 tbsp soy sauce (to taste)
- 1 tsp sesame oil (optional)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced (or 1/2 tsp garlic powder)
- 2 scallions (optional), sliced
- Black pepper; chili flakes/sriracha (optional)

Instructions
1) Prep: Break up cold rice so it’s not clumpy. Chop chicken.
2) Scramble eggs: Heat 1 tsp oil in a large skillet/wok over medium-high. Add eggs, scramble quickly, then remove to a plate.
3) Sauté: Add remaining oil. Cook garlic 15–30 seconds. Add vegetables and stir-fry 2–3 minutes (until hot).
4) Fry rice: Add rice. Press and toss to coat; cook 3–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it starts to toast.
5) Add chicken + season: Stir in chicken, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Cook 2 minutes until everything is hot. Add eggs back in.
6) Finish: Pepper to taste; top with scallions and optional chili.

Quick variations
- Add a tablespoon of oyster sauce or hoisin for sweetness.
- Swap soy sauce for teriyaki.
- Stir in leftover veggies (broccoli, bell pepper) near the end.

 Chess is a two-player game on an 8×8 board. White moves first; players alternate turns.

Objective:
- Win by checkmating the opponent’s king (the king is in check and has no legal move to escape).

Setup:
- Each side has 16 pieces: King, Queen, 2 Rooks, 2 Bishops, 2 Knights, 8 Pawns.
- Back rank (from a1 to h1 for White): Rook, Knight, Bishop, Queen, King, Bishop, Knight, Rook. (Queen on her own color.) Pawns fill the next rank.

How pieces move:
- King: 1 square any direction.
- Queen: any number of squares along rank/file/diagonal.
- Rook: any number along rank/file.
- Bishop: any number diagonally.
- Knight: “L” shape (2 then 1); can jump over pieces.
- Pawn: forward 1; from its start can move forward 2 if clear. Captures 1 square diagonally forward.

Capturing:
- Most pieces capture by moving to the target square. You cannot capture your own pieces.

Special rules:
- Check: your king is attacked; you must respond immediately (move king, capture attacker, or block if possible).
- Castling: king moves two squares toward a rook, rook jumps next to king. Allowed only if neither has moved, squares between are empty, king is not in check and does not pass through/land on attacked squares.
- En passant: if an enemy pawn moves two squares and lands beside your pawn, you may capture it as if it moved one square, but only on your very next move.
- Promotion: a pawn reaching the last rank becomes a Queen, Rook, Bishop, or Knight (usually Queen).

Draws (common):
- Stalemate (no legal move, not in check), threefold repetition, 50-move rule, insufficient mating material, or mutual agreement.

 Common reasons for fast battery drain and what to do:

1) High screen usage
- Causes: high brightness, long screen-on time, high refresh rate, always-on display.
- Fix: enable auto-brightness, lower brightness, reduce screen timeout, switch 120Hz→60Hz, disable always-on display, use dark mode (esp. OLED).

- Causes: social/media apps, VPNs, fitness trackers, games, malware-like adware.
- Fix: Settings → Battery/Power → Battery usage to find top drainers; force stop/uninstall suspicious apps; restrict background activity; disable “Background App Refresh” (iPhone) / background data (Android).

3) Location services (GPS)
- Causes: navigation, geofencing, “always” location permissions.
- Fix: set permissions to “While using,” turn off precise location where not needed, disable location history.

4) Poor signal / network and radios
- Causes: weak cellular signal makes the phone boost power; 5G searching; Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth scanning.
- Fix: use Wi‑Fi when possible; in bad reception areas enable Airplane mode temporarily; set 5G to “Auto/LTE” if appropriate; turn off Bluetooth/NFC when not used.

5) Notifications and syncing
- Causes: constant push notifications, email fetch, cloud sync.
- Fix: reduce notification frequency; set email to manual/less frequent fetch; limit auto-sync for nonessential accounts.

6) System/software issues
- Causes: OS update indexing, bugs, corrupted settings.
- Fix: restart; update OS/apps; check if drain started after a specific update/app install; try Safe Mode (Android) to test; as a last resort, back up and factory reset.

7) Battery aging or damage
- Causes: old battery, heat exposure.
- Fix: check Battery Health (iPhone) or battery diagnostics (Android); if health is low, replace the battery.

- Taxation and revenue measures after the French and Indian War (1763): Britain sought to pay war debts and fund troops in North America through acts like the Stamp Act (1765) and Townshend Duties (1767), provoking strong colonial opposition.

- Ideological influence: Enlightenment ideas about natural rights, consent of the governed, and republicanism—along with resistance literature and propaganda—helped justify breaking from Britain.

- Intercolonial unity and mobilization: Committees of correspondence, boycotts, and the First Continental Congress (1774) coordinated resistance, and fighting at Lexington and Concord (1775) turned political crisis into open war.

 The water cycle is how water moves around Earth over and over again:

1) Evaporation: The Sun warms water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. Some of it turns into water vapor (a gas) and rises into the air. Plants also release water vapor (transpiration).

2) Condensation: Higher up, the air is cooler. The water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny liquid droplets, forming clouds.

3) Precipitation: When the droplets in clouds join together and get heavy, they fall to the ground as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

4) Collection and runoff: The water gathers in rivers, lakes, oceans, and the ground (as groundwater). Some flows downhill as runoff back to bigger bodies of water.

Then the Sun heats it again, and the cycle repeats.

 A checking account is designed for everyday spending, while a savings account is designed for storing money and earning interest.

Checking account (spending account):
- Used for frequent transactions (paychecks, bills, debit card purchases).
- Usually comes with a debit card, checks, and bill pay.
- Typically low or no interest.
- Often has fewer limits on the number of withdrawals/transactions.

Savings account (money set aside):
- Used to save for goals or emergencies.
- Usually pays higher interest than checking (though rates vary).
- Limited spending tools (may not include checks; debit access may be limited).
- Banks may discourage frequent withdrawals and may charge fees if you exceed certain transaction limits.

Quick rule of thumb:
- Put money you need to spend regularly in checking.
- Put money you want to keep and grow (even modestly) in savings.

 Essential packing list for a 1-week hiking trip (adjust for weather, remoteness, and regulations):

1) Backpack & storage
- Backpack (50–70L typical) + rain cover

2) Shelter & sleep
- Tent/tarp + stakes/guylines (or hammock system)

- Sleeping pad (insulated if cold)

3) Clothing (layering)
- Moisture-wicking base layers
- Insulating layer (fleece/down)
- Waterproof/windproof shell jacket + rain pants
- Hiking pants/shorts; warm hat + sun hat; gloves if cold
- 3–5 pairs socks + underwear; camp clothes (optional)

4) Footwear
- Broken-in hiking boots/shoes
- Camp sandals/flip-flops (optional)

5) Water
- Water bottles/bladder (capacity to carry 2–4L depending on sources)

6) Food & cooking
- 7 days of calorie-dense food + 1 extra day buffer
- Stove + fuel (if allowed), lighter + backup matches
- Pot/mug/spoon; small knife
- Bear canister or hang kit if required; odor-proof bags

7) Navigation
- Map + compass (know how to use)
- GPS/phone offline maps + power bank

8) Safety & first aid
- First-aid kit (blister care is key)
- Headlamp + extra batteries
- Emergency bivy/space blanket
- Whistle; small repair kit (duct tape, needle/thread, cord)

9) Hygiene & toiletries
- Trowel + toilet paper/wipes (pack out if required)
- Hand sanitizer; toothbrush; small biodegradable soap
- Quick-dry towel

10) Sun/bug protection
